info.title: Detag API
info.description: Detag — watermark removal for images and videos you own. All errors are RFC 7807 problem+json with a stable PF-code (see the Problem schema).

get.summary:
Liveness: the process answers. Readiness (below) is the
dependency check.

Readiness (P0-035 db, P0-046 redis, P0-066 storage + models;
FR-X-02): 200 when every component is ok, 503 otherwise. The
four probes run concurrently — each is bounded by its own 2 s
timeout, so the worst case is ~2 s, not ~8 s. Every component
reports its probe latency in `latency_ms` (P0-066). The body is
always the same JSON — the status code is the signal, the body
is the diagnosis.

post.summary:
Register a user (P1-001, FR-A-01). Thin handler: the
service owns the flow; this maps its errors to the
problem+json envelope.

409.description: Email already registered (generic body — no enumeration detail)

422.description: Validation failed (email shape, password length, ToS version, disposable domain)

ComponentHealth.description:
One readiness component: a name, up/down, a safe detail
string, and the probe latency in milliseconds (P0-066).
`detail` never contains the database URL or credentials.
`latency_ms` is measured by the probe itself, from probe start
to the outcome — including the timeout path, so a slow
component reports a large latency instead of a missing one.
A sub-millisecond probe honestly reports 0.

FieldError.description:
One failed field in a 422 validation rejection (P0-101).

Serialized as an element of `Problem.field_errors`. The `message`
is generic by design — it never echoes the offending value — so
the list is safe to show in production, unlike `detail` (which
stays the variant's static safe text in production).

code.description:
Stable machine code, e.g. `invalid_email` — one per rule,
documented where the rule lives (`detag-validator`).

field.description: The request field that failed, e.g. `email`.

message.description: Human-readable message, e.g. `must be a valid email address`.

Problem.description: RFC 7807 problem body, as served by the api (`application/problem+json`).

detail.description:
Human-readable detail. In production this is always the variant's
static safe detail — never caller-supplied internals.

field_errors.description:
Per-field failures (P0-101). Present only on validation
rejections; omitted otherwise, so every other error body keeps
exactly the RFC 7807 fields the contract test locks.

request_id.description:
Echoed request id (UUIDv7); omitted when the caller has none yet
(request-id middleware lands in P0-019).

Readiness.description:
Overall readiness: `"ok"` only when every component is ok (and
at least one component was checked — an empty report is
`"degraded"`, never `"ok"`).

RegisterRequest.description:
The register request body (api-spec: email, password,
accept_tos_version → 201 user + verification email sent).

accept_tos_version.description:
The ToS version the user accepted; must equal the current
version (`PF_TOS_CURRENT_VERSION`, default "v1").

email.description: The email address (trimmed + lowercased before storage).

password.description:
The password (never trimmed, never logged, never stored —
only its Argon2id hash is).

UserResponse.description:
The register response: the created user, without the password
hash (there is no field for it — the type makes the leak
impossible, not just unlikely).
